newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Ashanti to spend $28 mln on exploration.
newsitem.headline: Ashanti to spend $28 mln on exploration.

text.p: Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Company Ltd will spend $28 million during 1997 on exploration with two-thirds of the funds earmarked for new greenfield locations, Ashanti Exploration managing director Peter Cowley said on Tuesday.
Cowley said at a sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals conference that one element of Ashanti's strategy was to build a high quality portfolio of gold properties in Africa.

"Over the last year, we have consolidated our exploration activities on the continent. We are currently active on some 35 projects in 12 countries and cover most of the prospective gold belts of West, East and Southern Africa," Cowley said.
He said the Geita project in Tanzania was Ashanti's most advanced exploration project. The mine produced nearly a million ounces of gold until the mid-sixties when it was closed.
"We are now calculating a revised resource at Geita which is expected to significantly increase on the current 1.3 million ounces.
"We are looking to Geita to become Ashanti's next major mine in Africa and our first in Tanzania," Cowley said.
With two new mines at Siguiri in Guinea and Bibiani in Ghana due to come on stream during 1998, Ashanti expected to lift gold output significantly.
"Thus, by the end of 1998, Ashanti's annual forecast gold production capacity will have increased by 60 percent to 1.4 million ounces over a three year period.
"Beyond 1999, we are looking to Geita in Tanzania and other projects in our exploration pipeline to further increase our production profile," Cowley said.
